About us

Tauranga is New Zealand’s fifth-largest city and one of the fastest‑growing. With beautiful beaches, a relaxed coastal lifestyle, and the dining, entertainment and shopping you’d expect from a vibrant urban centre, it’s easy to see why people from around the world choose to call Tauranga home. Tauranga City Council serves more than 162,000 residents. We maintain and develop the city’s infrastructure, deliver essential services, and invest in Tauranga’s future to ensure it remains a great place to live, work and play. As one of the region’s largest employers, we’re always looking for talented people to join our passionate, community-focused team. With more than 1,200 staff across a wide range of professions, there are plenty of opportunities to grow your career. Our roles span everything from building officers, planners, engineers and accountants to librarians, parks officers and environmental specialists. If you’re looking for a role where you can make a real difference in your community, explore our opportunities at careers.tauranga.govt.nz or get in touch with our team. Learn more about us at www.tauranga.govt.nz.

    Mauao landslide update Recent monitoring has confirmed more movement in the active landslide area above the Mount Maunganui Beachside Holiday Park. Six additional slip events have been recorded since last weekend. Safety controls, including the closure of Adams Avenue, remain in place while specialists continue to assess and monitor the site. Public safety remains the priority, and recovery efforts will continue to be guided by specialist advice. Repair works on Te Ara Tūtanga (base track) are continuing as planned. Please respect all barriers and signage and stay out of restricted areas.

    Over the weekend, further movement occurred at the site of the main landslide of 22 January 2026 within the Mount Maunganui Beachside Holiday Park. Geotechnical assessments and inspections on Mauao are continuing. We are currently unable to confirm whether Adams Avenue will reopen on Monday, 27 July. Access for residents and businesses has been retained via the southern footpath. Please do not linger in the area and follow any signage or directions from staff on site. We'll continue to provide updates as more information becomes available.

    Adams Avenue, between Pilot Bay and the Maunganui Road roundabout, is temporarily closed to vehicles, effective immediately. The closure is a precautionary measure following slips on Mauao overnight, while geotechnical engineers assess the site. It is expected to remain in place until at least Monday, 27 July. Please avoid the area and follow any signage or directions from staff on site. We appreciate your patience and will provide updates as more information becomes available.
